one_liner: Twilio has a broad, self-serve REST API (1,800+ endpoints) with API keys/Basic and OAuth 2.0; free trial gives credentials immediately; the official MCP is docs-only, with an official-labelled open-source alpha MCP that executes API calls.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 apps support client credentials and authorization code grants (token endpoint oauth.twilio.com/v2/token). API keys (Main/Standard/Restricted) and Account SID/Auth Token are used via HTTP Basic. Access Tokens (JWT) are for client SDKs only.
access_notes: Free 30-day trial without credit card gives working Account SID/Auth Token and API keys; trial has restrictions and limited free units, then pay-as-you-go usage pricing. Could arguably be viewed as self_serve_free, but trial expires after 30 days.
blocker_notes: Trial accounts have restrictions and expire in 30 days, but credentials and API work immediately; paid usage is only needed for production use.

You can sign up for a Twilio free trial account without a credit card. Trial accounts expire after 30 days.
There are no separate trial-only credentials. Trial restrictions are enforced by your account status, not by different credentials.
